original_question: Let #P(*, e, t) denote the number of pure O-sequences of socle degree e and type t. For fixed e, determine the asymptotic behavior of #P(*, e, t) as t becomes large; in particular, what is the correct order of magnitude of #P(*, e, t)?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Open Problem 5, read together with Section 4's definition of P(*,e,t) and Theorem 4.6, and Section 2's definition of pure O-sequence and type. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation: it uses the correct notation #P(*,e,t), fixes e and lets t grow, and asks for the asymptotic behavior and order of magnitude. This is essentially the wording of Open Problem 5. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
missing_details: The star in P(*,e,t) should be explained: codimension is not fixed, unlike the notation P(r,e,t) used earlier in Section 4. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

The object being counted is the set of pure O-sequences (that is, h-vectors), not isomorphism classes of algebras or monomial order ideals. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
A pure O-sequence should be defined explicitly as the h-vector of a pure monomial order ideal. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
The equivalent algebraic formulation should be stated: these are Hilbert functions of standard graded artinian monomial level algebras. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
Type t should be defined as the number of maximal monomials in the pure order ideal, equivalently the K-dimension of the socle. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

The socle degree e should be identified with the common degree of the maximal monomials, equivalently the degree in which the socle is concentrated. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
The quantifiers should be made explicit: e and t are positive integers, e is fixed, and the limit is taken as t tends to infinity. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
To be fully stand-alone, one should note that P(*,e,t) is finite for fixed e and t. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

If one wants the question to reflect the paper's live open content rather than restate known cases, one should note that the case e=3 is already solved by Theorem 4.6, so the unsolved extension is mainly for e>=4. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))

The field/background ring can be specified: one works over a polynomial ring K[x1,...,xr] (or K[y1,...,yr]) over a field K, and the paper notes that being a pure O-sequence is independent of the choice of K. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
refined_question: For each fixed positive integer e, let P(*,e,t) denote the finite set of h-vectors h=(1,h1,...,he) that occur as Hilbert functions of standard graded artinian monomial level algebras A=K[x1,...,xr]/I, where r is allowed to vary, I is a monomial ideal, and the socle soc(A)=0:_A(x1,...,xr) is concentrated in degree e and has K-dimension t; equivalently, P(*,e,t) is the set of pure O-sequences of socle degree e and type t over all codimensions. Determine, as t tends to infinity, the asymptotic behavior of #P(*,e,t), and in particular the correct order of magnitude of #P(*,e,t). ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for each fixed positive integer e, count up to equality of h-vector the pure monomial order ideals in K[y1,...,yr], with r varying, whose maximal monomials all have degree e and whose number of maximal monomials is t; determine the asymptotic growth of this count as t tends to infinity. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Open Problem 5 in Section 5 almost verbatim. Section 4 introduces the notation P(*,e,t) as the finite set of pure O-sequences of socle degree e and type t, after first distinguishing the fixed-codimension notation P(r,e,t) in Proposition 4.3, and it records the solved benchmark e=3 in Theorem 4.6. Section 2 provides the precise definitions of pure O-sequence, socle degree, type, and the equivalent formulation via standard graded artinian monomial level algebras. So the faithful sharpening is mainly to spell out those definitions and the meaning of the star while keeping the problem exactly at the paper's scope. ([www3.nd.edu](https://www3.nd.edu/~jmiglior/MNZ5POSexp.pdf))
